messages.subject: Scale/axes with geom_treescale() vs theme_tree2()
parts: I am trying to understand the different scales that you get between using geom_treescale() and theme_tree2().  I have a 10x10 distance matrix that has been single-linkage clustered, and drawing the trees shows different scales with the two methods.  Neither seems to be in line with what I would expect based on the $heights attribute of the hclust object.  Can anyone point me in the direction of understanding this?  Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 9f3bd015c1bf00a0
messages.subject: Re: Scale/axes with geom_treescale() vs theme_tree2()
parts:
For anyone who comes across this in the future, it is due to how ggtree uses ape::as.phylo (or similar) to convert a cluster object into a tree.  There is a note on the man page for as.phylo that says: 
"In an object of class "hclust", the height gives the distance between the two sets that are being agglomerated. So these distances are divided by two when setting the branch lengths of a phylogenetic tree."

See also this post: https://r-sig-phylo.r-project.narkive.com/dUNP7St0/as-phylo-hclust
